card: Adds a `-walletrebroadcast` configuration option defaulting to false, decoupling periodic wallet rebroadcasts from initial transaction broadcasts. Currently, rebroadcasting unconfirmed transactions every 12 to 36 hours advertises wallet ownership to peers, with no way to disable it without turning off initial broadcasts entirely. Disabling rebroadcast also skips reloading unconfirmed wallet transactions into the local mempool during startup.
changed_since_previous: Now includes full patch details showing the option definition, test updates, and parameter interaction setting `-walletrebroadcast=0` when `-blocksonly=1`.
evidence: PR description: 'Rebroadcasting transactions that are already known to the network reveals that the wallet is related to them. The way this is done (periodically send to everybody) could have bad implications for privacy... Before this PR -walletbroadcast controlled both the initial broadcast and the subsequent periodic rebroadcasts'.
problem: Periodic rebroadcasting of unconfirmed transactions every 12 to 36 hours announces transactions to all connected peers, which leaks to the network that the node's wallet is the sender or receiver. Users previously had no way to turn off these periodic rebroadcasts without also disabling initial transaction broadcasting via `-walletbroadcast`.

risk.why: Defaulting rebroadcast to false changes node behavior so stuck or evicted unconfirmed transactions will not automatically be rebroadcast, potentially leaving user transactions unconfirmed if network peers drop them.

scope_notes: The check for `-walletrebroadcast` replaces `-walletbroadcast` in `CWallet::ResubmitWalletTransactions`, which also gates non-broadcasting resubmission of unconfirmed transactions to the local mempool on startup.
summary: Adds a `-walletrebroadcast` configuration option to decouple unconfirmed transaction rebroadcasts from initial transaction broadcasts. Setting `-walletrebroadcast=false` (the new default) disables periodic rebroadcasts every 12–36 hours as well as wallet transaction resubmission to the local mempool on startup, while leaving initial transaction broadcast controlled by `-walletbroadcast`.
